Tool names here are Academic Harness's own. In Claude Code, `subagent` is `Agent`, `skill` is `Skill`, `ask_user_question` is `AskUserQuestion`, and `mcp__papermemory__*` is `mcp__plugin_academic-harness_papermemory__*`. If a tool named below is not in your tool list, say so.

## Deep review

`deep_review` runs a vendored Open Deep Review engine over a full manuscript: multi-pass segmented critique, page/quote-anchored comments, a scholar-peer summary with questions for authors, and reference verification. Use it when the user asks for a Deep-Review-style, multi-pass, or pre-submission critique, or wants a second opinion on a whole paper. Whenever the user asks for a paper or manuscript review, critique, referee report, feedback, assessment, or pre-submission check — including a plain "review this paper" — do not assume the normal path. Ask which they want, and spell out the deep option because the user may not know it exists: deep review (multi-pass engine, page/quote-anchored comments, author questions, reference checks; takes minutes) or a normal session review (fast session-model critique/referee report). Present the choice every time a paper review is requested unless the user explicitly asks for deep review or has already chosen a mode in this conversation; then act on their choice. Routine section edits, a reporting checklist, or a referee report the user explicitly wants written in this session do not need the engine. It runs on the session's current model through the host LLM service — the same provider and model as the chat, so switching the session model switches the reviewer. Confirm the scope and expected duration with the user before `review`; never run a review unprompted. `estimate` is optional and only needed when the user asks for an engine-run estimate. The run is stateful: artifacts live under `.dsh/deep-review/<key>/`, `review` returns only a compact summary, and `show` reads back the summary, comments, questions, checklist, claims, citations, rounds, or the full Markdown. `status` reports a stored review as stale when the manuscript has changed. Every `review` is kept as a numbered round, so after the user revises and agrees to another review, call `compare` to see which findings closed, opened, or changed severity and how claims, checklist items, and citations moved. Read it with the two limits it states: findings are paired by wording, then wording similarity, then the quoted span — comment ids are tried first but the engine re-issues them per run, so ids rarely match, and `compare` prints a `Matched by` line naming the rule that paired each finding, because a closed finding is a lead, not proof the science improved — and when `compare` reports that the manuscript bytes did not change, everything that moved between the rounds is reviewer variance, which you must name as such before crediting the revision with anything. Never turn the ladder into a score to climb or present it as an acceptance decision. `validity` asks the four evaluation-validity questions the engine's critique leaves open, over a stored round and a deterministic count of the manuscript itself: `attribution` (does the text carry a removal arm for a claimed gain, or only generic training controls), `evaluator_drift` (is a stated before-and-after value change located in the evaluation harness rather than in the model), `benchmark_coverage` (how many metric axes, other axes, and baseline-like arms the results grid actually has), and `unmeasured_trade_off` (is a quality or feasibility counter-metric reported beside a speed, memory, or iteration gain). Each answers `clear`, `flagged`, or `not_checked`: a `flagged` state names an absence in the text, not a flaw in the work, and `not_checked` is not a pass — it is the honest answer when the manuscript carries too little to judge, so never report it as sound. Counting is keyword and grid based, and the vocabularies and cut-offs are the plugin's own, not the paper's. The action makes at most one model call — a critic on the session route that can annotate a finding but never change its state — and `critic: false` makes none. Read it with `show` section `validity`; it writes `extra_checks.json` beside the review and records its own `notebook` entry tagged `validity`; do not duplicate that entry yourself. `provenance_audit` indexes `extra_checks.json` (a `flagged` check appears as an `unverified` claim, and `arms` reports the flags); these readings gate nothing, and only `ah_check` blocks. Use `review` for the systematic-review ledger and `reporting_check` for guideline compliance; delegate a referee report written by this session's model to the `peer-reviewer` subagent. Report each finding's anchored page or line, and treat the output as advisory criticism, not verified fact. `score` reads a stored round and returns four advisory dimension readings (soundness, originality, clarity, significance) on a declared scale, each citing stored comment ids; it makes one bounded model call, dimensions without a valid citation are not_checked, and the number is never an acceptance decision or a gate. Report the scale, the cited comment ids, and whether the round is held_out or in_distribution; pass rubric_round when a prior round's rubric or report fed the revision so the next round is recorded in_distribution. Settings hold the default rubric, the review round limit, and the per-review spend ceiling; the Phase 0 calibration harness correlates stored scores with real decisions and reports not_checked below its sample floor. Load the `deep-review` skill for the workflow.
